reviewer: independent review agent (did not write plan.json, did not deploy, did not commit, no purchasing/outreach)
evidence: Code reading + numerical-uncalibrated re-runs on a PATCHED SCRATCH COPY of sim/ (repo sim/ untouched). Simulation is not physical verification. No physical test was run; M-070 not_run; G-MATURE stays closed. User panel is SIMULATED personas, not real users.

method.reproduction: 48-case FULLRUN_CASES_R4 ensemble re-run at defaults on a copy: every judged number reproduced exactly (avail 47.368, jitter p90 4.04, azRange 40.075, KE 15.358, headClear 0.075, endurance 45.142) -> review/baseline_repro.json
method.variants: review/variants.jsonl, produced by scripts/run_variants.sh -> scripts/rev_ens.mjs on a copy patched by scripts/patch_copy.py (REV_JSON switches; defaults unchanged when switches are off)
method.handCalcs: scripts/geometry_levers.py -> geometry_levers.out.txt (shared bodyPoints geometry, q range, KE)

verdictSummary.reviewVerdict: 7/13 pass after correcting one optimistic bug (48 MP camera power/mass omitted): endurance flips PASS->FAIL (45.1 -> 43.3 min) and KE worsens 15.4 -> 16.3 J. Conclusion 'not a usable design' is CONFIRMED and slightly stronger. No failing criterion flips to pass under a fair correction. KE can be flipped to pass by a design lever (tailwind envelope and/or -8 % kite mass), headClear cannot without a stand-off (pole) or a user rule change, and even a relaxed line rule would still fail on tailwind stops.

flips.to: FAIL 43.29 min (48 MP +0.5 W/+3 g, activetether basis) / 42.16 min (towglider fix48 basis 3.5 W)
PASS 13.65 J with a tailwind launch envelope (no launch / retrieve when est. tailwind > 6 m/s), avail cost -3.7 pt (47.4 -> 43.7 %); PASS 14.03 J with kite mass -8 %; PASS 12.40 J with both

findings.title: 48 MP camera power (+0.5 W) and mass not counted on the pod
findings.evidence: design.js CAMERA.src says '48 MP ... same mass as cam4kNoGimbal +0.5 W', but POD_ITEMS uses cam4kNoGimbal (27 g, 2.7 W) only; analysis uses the 8000x6000 sensor for px. towglider fix48 basis is 30 g / 3.5 W. activetether has the same omission (consistent but wrong).
findings.verdict: endurance PASS -> FAIL; KE fails by more (16.3 J). Fix: count the 48 MP module honestly and add ~+20-25 g of pack battery (team's own note) — re-judge; also apply to activetether for fairness.

findings.title: Line passes 7.5 cm from the helmet centre in tailwind stops; a split 'line >= X m' rule would not rescue the design
findings.evidence: Worst headClear cases are all RETRIEVE in tailwind: tail4.5_s11 0.075 m (39.6 s), tail4.5_s13 0.149, tail5.5_s13 0.212. 13/48 cases have line-to-helmet < 0.5 m (14/48 with corrected camera). The kite is blown over/ahead of the stopping rider and the line crosses the head/neck. With a ~0.13 m helmet radius this is line-on-helmet/neck contact at up to 38 N (weak link) — a laceration/strangulation-class hazard, not a clearance shortfall.
findings.verdict: BRIEF option (a) 'flyer >=1.0 m unchanged; line >= X m with weak link' fails for any X >= ~0.1 m unless tailwind stop behaviour is redesigned. Must be stated to the user alongside the rule-change option.

findings.title: Flyer >= 1.0 m also fails in most cases at the launch, not only the line
findings.evidence: headFlyer < 1.0 m in 48/48 cases (max 0.956 m). The kite starts at the sacrum mouth, |mouth-helmet| = 0.98 m in the shared body model. The analysis draws the OPEN sail outline (0.59 m span) while the sail is still folded (pessimistic); with a folded 0.46 m bundle while collapsed, flyer < 1.0 m still in 36/48 cases (min 0.43 m, p10 0.88).
findings.verdict: Pessimistic outline at launch is a real modelling error (fix: draw a folded bundle while collapsed) but it does not flip anything. The flyer part of headClear fails because launch and non-final capture start inside 1 m; only a launch-window exclusion (rule change, user decision) or a stand-off changes this.

findings.title: Camera attitude-drift model differs from activetether (0.2 Hz low-pass vs raw OU)
findings.evidence: analysis.js low-passes the drift; activetether keeps the raw 50 Hz OU. Re-run with the activetether model: jitter p90 4.04 -> 6.43 deg/s (calm worse too).
findings.verdict: Physically the low-pass is the more plausible model (team disclosed it), and the sledpack verdict does not flip. But the cross-concept comparison is no longer like-for-like: either re-judge activetether with the same drift model or report sledpack with both. Integrator decision; do not quote 4.0 vs AT-1's 10.5 as a design gain without this caveat.

findings.title: azRange is natural wander, not a 'commandable' span
findings.evidence: Criterion: 'p5-p95 span of viewing azimuth deliverable on command'. sledpack has no steering command (activetether has azShot); its 40 deg median is uncontrolled swing (head ~18-20 deg, tail 100-147 deg because the kite swings round the window).
findings.verdict: The honest commandable span is ~0 deg; criterion fails more clearly than reported. Large tail-case values must not be presented as a feature.

findings.title: 0.50 m sleeve cannot hold pod + 0.457 m spars + drogue cone + 1.2 m tail line + bridle
findings.evidence: pod 45 mm + spar length 457 mm = 0.502 m > 0.50 m sleeve (I8 shortened it from 0.60 m); the 0.25 m drogue cone and 1.2 m tail line and both bridles also have to go in. A 0.65-0.70 m sleeve adds 0.42-0.57 L.
findings.verdict: packVol could become marginal/FAIL (3.0 L limit); a 0.70 m spine sleeve also reaches above the shoulder blades toward the helmet. Needs a stow-length budget.

findings.title: Passing endurance and failing-by-a-little KE are not robust
findings.evidence: team sensitivity.json: endurance fails with CD0 +20 % (43.5), wind-bias -2 (43.1), experts (31-41 min); KE 18.1 J on seeds 14-16 and 18.5 J at wind-bias +2. 'Just above 14.9 J' is a single-seed-set statement.
findings.verdict: Treat KE as a clear fail (15-23 J range) and endurance as a fail-at-margin until the battery is resized.

findings.title: Launch extraction, rider wake, tail/line entanglement not modelled
findings.evidence: At launch the kite is placed 0.08 m outside the mouth with no sleeve friction/extraction; the skier's turbulent wake (rider at 12 m/s, bundle at 0.1-3 m behind the sacrum) and snow spray are not modelled; drogue tail and three lines from one mouth can twist; tow-in near skis not modelled. Launch success 95.3 % and dock 96.5 % (ASSUMED capture model) are therefore upper-bound-ish.
findings.verdict: Keep these numbers labelled as model outputs with assumed sub-models; kill tests listed in REPORT.md are the right ones.

findings.title: Sensor-fit check is vacuous (offAx = 0)
findings.evidence: analysis.js sets offAx = 0 so the crop is never checked against the pod's real optical axis. Re-run with the crop required to fit the 66 deg sensor around the low-passed line-direction axis: avail 47.37 -> 47.12 %.
findings.verdict: Bug in principle, negligible in effect; fix for honesty.

findings.title: collapses metric undercounts emergency flag-outs; MANUAL release and refusal accounting read truth 'riding'
findings.evidence: collapses mean 0 while collapseShare mean 0.49 % (max 20 %) — the >30 N emergency flag-out sets collapsed without counting. model.js MODE.MANUAL uses ridingAt() (truth) to finish a manual stow; manual = 0 in all 48 so no judged effect.
findings.verdict: No verdict effect; fix for traceability.

findings.title: Shared rules applied as for other concepts
findings.evidence: Gates use the shared windEstimate() + noisy GNSS (no oracle); helmet = shared bodyPoints().head; headClear excludes only the last <=3 s of each capture window; KE rider-frame within 1.5 m of helmet/exit, ground frame beyond; artefact rule = shared artefactCounts (>=2 px); avail over col.riding with refusals = 0; reel/depower drum rate- and force-limited; tension/angle/length sensors have noise, bias, latency; tracker uses vision with dropouts + biased geometry. Mild idealisation: the geometry aim estimate uses the true line direction + a fixed bias instead of the noisy measured cM and ignores sag (fused with vision; low impact).

findings.title: Sled polar plausible; drogue tail is an un-depowerable 12 N at 22 m/s
findings.evidence: AR 1.73, CLa 2.34/rad (Helmbold), CLmax 1.0, CD0 0.12, e 0.7 -> L/D max of the sail 2.8; with tail CdA 0.05 on S 0.20 (dCD 0.25) the effective L/D at CL ~0.7 is ~1.4 -> ~55 deg line angle, consistent with sled practice (45-60 deg). Tail drag at 22 m/s = 0.5*1.0*22^2*0.05 = 12.1 N of the 35.9 N body-force peak and cannot be depowered. Zero in-flight collapse events in 48 cases with +/-7 m/s lateral carving is optimistic for a single-skin sled (sleds are known to fold in lulls/side-slip); collapse thresholds are ASSUMED.
findings.verdict: Coefficients plausible within ASSUMED status; collapse robustness is the weakest aero assumption.

rootCauseClaims.verdict: CONFIRMED (geometry), but why_pole.py's 0.52-0.69 m understates the SHARED body model: |sacrum mouth - helmet| = 0.97-0.99 m (crouch 0.2-0.6). At the 55 deg filming elevation the line passes 0.82-0.85 m from the helmet; it reaches ~|d| only for a line ~23-25 deg above horizontal behind (perpendicular to the exit-helmet vector). Kite overhead (90 deg) -> 0.37-0.41 m; kite blown forward over the head (110 deg) -> 0.04-0.08 m, which is the actual binding case. 1.0 m at 55 deg needs the exit >= ~0.45 m behind the sacrum (stand-off = a pole) or 0.3 m lower AND 0.3 m further back.

rootCauseClaims.claim: Dynamic pressure spans ~30x but a sled varies its force coefficient only 3-4x
rootCauseClaims.verdict: CONFIRMED in direction. q = 8 Pa (4 m/s) to 242 Pa (22 m/s) = 30x; above the 5.5 m/s gate 16x. With the 14 deg AoA collapse margin the sail resultant coefficient spans only ~2-3x, and the drogue tail adds a non-depowerable 12 N at 22 m/s. Hence 36 N peak against a 38 N weak link.

rootCauseClaims.claim: Tailwind: carving lateral speed dominates the airflow direction
rootCauseClaims.verdict: CONFIRMED. At psi 45 deg and 12 m/s the rider's along-track/lateral components are ~8.5/8.5 m/s; in a 6 m/s tailwind the along-track apparent wind falls to ~2.5 m/s and the apparent-wind direction swings ~+/-70 deg each turn. Tail cases avail 32 %, azRange 100-147 deg, all worst headClear cases are tail.

rootCauseClaims.claim: KE floor: the kite moves at least at rider speed
rootCauseClaims.verdict: CONFIRMED but not binding: floor 0.5*0.0674*12^2 = 4.9 J (recreational), 8.6 J at 16 m/s. The fails are whip/tailwind ground speed ~21 m/s (cap for 14.9 J at 67.4 g is 21.0 m/s) — mass and envelope are the levers.

rootCauseClaims.claim: bodyPx falls when carving lean is seen from 55 deg above
rootCauseClaims.verdict: PLAUSIBLE (bodyPx median 389 passes; <300 px frames are a share of the avail loss). Line length is NOT a lever: 9 m line -> pxMed 340, avail 38.0 %, KE 18.8 J, headClear 0.003 m, endurance 43.0 (all worse).

missedLevers.lever: Tailwind operating envelope (no launch / early retrieve when estimated tailwind along the track > 6 m/s)
missedLevers.note: Honest product behaviour; must be disclosed as 'does not fly in strong tailwind'.

missedLevers.lever: Kite mass -8 % (67.4 -> 62 g), e.g. lighter camera module or less margin

effect.keMax: 14.03 J PASS (but seeds 14-16 / expert riders would still fail)
effect.headClear: 0.011 m (worse in one capture case; chaotic)

missedLevers.lever: Camera on the line below the kite (KAP/Picavet-style pod 1-2 m down the line) instead of at the bridle apex
missedLevers.effect: Splits the strike bodies: sail+tail 18 g -> 4.1 J at the worst 21.4 m/s; pod 49 g <= 11.3 J even at kite speed (lower in practice, it sits nearer the rider). KE would pass by a wide margin under the shared per-body rule (activetether already judges flyer and pod separately). Picavet also damps pendulum jitter. Costs: line in the onboard view (0.3 mm line at <0.5 m from the lens can exceed 2 px), pod now nearer the head (worse for headClear), docking two bodies.

missedLevers.lever: Narrower lens (e.g. 50 deg instead of 66 deg) on the 48 MP sensor
missedLevers.effect: ~1.3x native px per degree -> allows a lower elevation (~45 deg, less lean-from-above px loss, line clearance 0.91 vs 0.84 m) at the same bodyPx; costs framing margin in carving swing.

missedLevers.lever: Lower flying angle (~45 deg) via bigger tail/bridle trim
missedLevers.status: HYPOTHESIS + partly tested by team (I7 tail x1.6 avail 49 %, tail cases worse)
missedLevers.effect: Line-at-55 clearance 0.84 -> 0.91 m (still < 1.0); worse clothesline (line <2 m above snow further behind).

missedLevers.note: A 0.13 m rearward stand-off already behaves like a mini-boom and is a chairlift/fall hazard; 1.0 m needs ~0.45 m.

missedLevers.lever: Tailwind-stop strategy: at a stop with est. tailwind, free-spool and let the depowered kite land downwind and to the side (rider stops across the slope) then tow in low, instead of reeling a kite that is above/ahead past the head
missedLevers.effect: Targets the binding 0.075-0.21 m RETRIEVE cases; geometry: a line running forward-low from the sacrum stays ~0.9-0.95 m from the helmet (still < 1.0 m by the 0.98 m bound).

missedLevers.lever: Battery +20-25 g (or a real 18650 energy density instead of the shared 150 Wh/kg)
missedLevers.effect: +3 Wh -> endurance ~52 min with the corrected camera power; mass 0.60 kg still far below 1.5 kg.

missedLevers.lever: Different soft kite: two-line (or 3-line) steerable foil / parafoil with pack-side steering
missedLevers.effect: Only lever that creates a COMMANDABLE azimuth (azRange) and actively holds the kite out of the head zone in tailwind stops; a foil has a wider force-coefficient range via brakes (helps RV-12) but launches/docks worse from a sleeve and collapses more easily. Needs its own model.

missedLevers.lever: User-level rule options (user decision, do NOT change shared criteria)
missedLevers.effect: headClear split (flyer >= 1.0 m outside launch+capture windows; line >= X m with weak link) — even with it, current design fails because of tailwind stops (RV-02) and launch (RV-03).

copyAudit.overall: Mostly honest: global tag, onboard label, HUD 'scripted values', end disclaimer and a 'still open' block exist. Problems: (1) 'still open' omits two failing criteria (jitter, azRange) and the endurance that fails after RV-01; (2) the facts block titled 'what already works in simulation' mixes design estimates and an ASSUMED capture model and includes a dock rate that FAILS the team's own >=98 % product target; (3) several section titles state untested behaviour as fact ('It knows', 'It docks itself', 'Ski, and it flies'); (4) the KE line minimises ('just above'); (5) the safety nature of the 0.075 m line clearance is not stated.

recommendedDesignChanges: 1. Fix RV-01 (48 MP power/mass) and add ~20-25 g of pack battery; re-run and re-judge (also activetether).

2. Tailwind envelope (no launch / early retrieve at est. tailwind > ~6 m/s) + a tailwind-stop strategy that never reels a high/forward kite past the head; disclose 'does not fly in strong tailwind'. Envelope alone flips KE (13.6 J) at -3.7 pt avail.
3. Evaluate a line-mounted camera pod (KAP/Picavet) below a ~18 g sled: separates strike bodies (KE ~4 J sail / <=11 J pod) and damps jitter — needs a model.
4. Fix the stow-length budget (sleeve >= 0.65-0.70 m or a shorter/foldable tail) and re-check packVol and the sleeve top vs the helmet.

5. Report to the user, as options not decisions: headClear cannot pass without a ~0.45 m stand-off; a split rule still fails until RV-02/RV-03 are fixed; azRange is ~0 commandable without a steerable (multi-line) kite.
6. Make the drift model the same across concepts (RV-04) before any cross-concept comparison is shown to the user.
